chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The waiting period of the woman who gives Khul'a is similar to the waiting period of the divorced woman, and her Khul'a is her divorce.

key_terms.المُخْتَلِعَةِ: The woman who gives Khul'a (divorce initiated by wife)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman who undergoes Khul'a divorce?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the 'Iddah of a woman undergoing Khul'a mirrors that of a standard Talaq, affirming the juristic consensus that Khul'a functions as a revocable divorce rather than a distinct contractual dissolution. This ruling, recorded in al-Kafi, underscores the practical implication that the wife remains in her marital home during the waiting period, ensuring continuity in financial support and potential reconciliation. The hadith highlights the Shia scholarly view that the procedural mechanics of Khul'a align closely with Talaq, distinguishing it from Mubara'at.
